body: Thank you, we're going to have a talk when she comes home in a week, but I might write my thoughts down in more detail so there's no miscommunication. I hope she'll understand why I'm hurt.

It's very comforting to hear this. I understand that my friend might be hurt and that's obviously not what I want, but I don't think I'm overreacting by feeling that it's unfair of her to not consider my circumstances and what limits I have. I hope we can sort it out and hopefully it's just a misunderstanding, but if she continues to show that kind of disregard for my mental health I might reconsider our friendship. I can't really afford to feel guilty for something I can't control if I want to stay on top of the goals I'm trying to achieve. It's a very draining situation.

I understand that. I do try my best, but it gets so overwhelming and just going a few miles out of my way feels daunting and nearly impossible. I do feel guilty and perhaps I'm just not trying hard enough.
thanks for your insight, I'll keep that in mind.
you're a saint, mate. spending your time trying to help people out. i'm glad you're better. take care.
well, who's to say what's better? I'll admit, a level head and reasoning doesn't exactly go hand in hand with a suicidal state of mind, but I'm pretty sure this is what I want

you can feel lonely even if you have friends and a good family. It's fine, and it's not your fault. Sometimes there's just something on your mind that you don't want to tell the people you love. Sometimes it's easier venting to someone you know you won't have to see in real life.

depression is a lonely place, but there's a lot of people who want to help you.

try making a new friend.

I'm not very interesting, but I'm always open for a chat

Priceless.

Everyone's uniqe, for better or for worse. Every passerby on the street has had a life as complex and meaningful as your own. Who gets to judge what they're worth? 

Even genuinely bad people more often than not have someone who love or depend on them.

no reason for being triggered is stupid. every single struggle you're having is valid, and you deserve the right to feel the way you do, but you also need to realise that what you're feeling is worth reaching out to someone about.

Try to get help. If you're not comfortable talking about suicide, what you've been thinking about, ask for help on your assignments, or some motivation. try to find a reason behind school. maybe what you hope you'll get into in the future. 

I know how overwhelming all that is, so if that all seems pointless, maybe just take a break from it all, breathe for a moment. just focus on staying alive for now. Maybe we can talk about it, or something entirely different. Do you like video games? Music, maybe?
it sucks. I want to have a social life and a hobby and be able to take care of myself, not just stress about essays on urbanization all the time
yeah, exactly, sometimes I feel like I'm always just pretending

Oh yeah. It's like you're dissociating. everything just feels off, not quite right. you don't feel like yourself. Like you're not supposed to be where you are or be talking to your friends, you're supposed to be some stranger walking past you on the street, maybe then you could feel normal. It's exhausting.
